content.title: Dirty dozen produce 2026: list
content.text: by: Talia Naquin Posted: Mar 24, 2026 / 11:36 AM EDT Updated: Mar 24, 2026 / 01:52 PM EDT (WJW) – A lot of popular fruit and vegetables continue to carry pesticide residues, including PFAS “forever chemicals.” That’s according to the Environmental Working Group’s 2026 Shopper’s Guide to Pesticides in Produce. It’s better known as the Dirty Dozen report. Leading the list are spinach, kale, collard and mustard greens, followed by strawberries, grapes, and nectarines. Blackberries, which were newly tested, averaged more than four pesticides per sample. Apples, cherries, pears and potatoes were also in the dirty dozen. Key findings for the Dirty Dozen: 96% of samples contained pesticides. 203 different pesticides were detected. Most items averaged four or more pesticides per sample. “Consumers have a right to know what’s on their food,” said Varun Subramaniam, a science analyst at EWG. “This year’s findings underscore the presence of PFAS pesticides in the food supply. Clean Fifteen The lowest pesticide residues make up the Clean Fifteen list. Here’s what’s on it: Pineapple, sweet corn, and avocados top the list, followed by papaya, onions, frozen sweet peas, asparagus, cabbage, cauliflower, watermelon, mangoes, bananas, carrots, mushrooms, and kiwi. Key findings for the Clean Fifteen: Nearly 60% of samples had no detectable pesticide residues. Only 16% contained two or more pesticides. See the rankings here.
